search_log: Searched: Tom Hanks Uncommon Type first person third person stories point of view review.
Searched authorized excerpts using Penguin Random House, Penguin UK, Guardian, One Story, and New Yorker queries.

Opened and inspected Penguin’s 43-page publisher sample, the Guardian’s complete “Three Exhausting Weeks,” One Story’s “A Month on Greene Street” excerpt, and the Hanks–Patrick Ryan interview reproduced by Parnassus Musing.

Checked Kirkus and publisher descriptions for collection structure; Kirkus corroborated an unnamed first-person narrator across three recurring-character stories but did not alone establish the third-person strand.
Found a BookRags point-of-view summary but did not rely on it because stronger authorized and author-interview evidence was available.
person_note: This eligible prose collection alternates at book level because different complete stories use different controlling persons. The quote set independently contains sustained first-person narration involving Anna and the recurring friends, plus sustained third-person narration involving Sue and Bob Roy. Tier A excerpts verify a complete first-person story and a third-person story, while a commercial repost of an author/editor interview explicitly describes both modes across the collection. First-person words inside Sue/Bob dialogue and generic uses of “you” are local material, not additional base strands. Confidence is medium because the collection-level structural source is Tier C even though the two constituent modes are confirmed by authorized excerpts.
